chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the divorced woman,

her husband divorces her but he does not let her know except after a year. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If two just witnesses come, she should not observe the waiting period, or else let her observe it from the day it reaches her'.
ai.seo_question: How long is the waiting period for a divorced woman if her husband was absent and she only found out later?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of iddah (waiting period) for a mu'allaq (conditional or delayed) divorce when the wife is unaware of the event, establishing that the period begins upon notification unless corroborated by two just witnesses. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and the practical reality of communication delays in marital law, ensuring the woman is not burdened with an indefinite waiting period without proof. It underscores the role of witness testimony in validating the timing of the divorce decree relative to the wife's knowledge.
